gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured figure for any of its picks. The only bench number this angle could source is BudgetLightForum reviewer Budda's reading of 'basically 10A' of charging current from the NOCO GENIUS10, which matches its 10 A rating.
standout_why: I opened williamswordsmith.com/best-trolling-motor-battery-charger (2026-10-21). It ranks 10 chargers using only rated or listing figures and names no tester. WebFetch failed on gearranking.com/marine-chargers, gearranking.com/marine-chargers/lithium and boatdealsdirect.com with a self-signed certificate error, and the shell download was not allowed, so I could not check those three for measured data. ChatGPT's two answers and its cited Minn Kota help pages and no.co spec page give only rated amps per bank. Budda's 10 A reading is new as a measurement but only confirms the 10 A rating the rivals already print.
decides: It does not change the pick. It confirms that the portable NOCO GENIUS10 delivers its rated 10 A, so a 100 Ah trolling battery takes about 10 h at full current (100 Ah ÷ 10 A, before the taper). No named bench test exists for the onboard picks (NOCO GENPRO10X3, Minn Kota MK-330PCL / MK-345PCL / MK-318PCL, NOCO GEN5X3). The page can say plainly that no independent lab has published output or charge-time data for these onboard chargers, and should not imply that any 'tested' ranking exists.
